open_points.subject: StaffProjectAssignment for an administrator
open_points.text: M07 says, “The assignment operation accepts any existing staff account; an assignment naming an administrator has no effect, because authorization never consults assignments for the administrator role.” State 0 invariant 4 says, “Revoked membership/grant blocks new requests immediately,” and R0-24 says an existing staff assignment “keeps giving read access” and may be revoked.
open_points.question: Is an administrator’s StaffProjectAssignment intentionally inert, or must creating and revoking every StaffProjectAssignment grant and remove project access?
options: Assignments may be created for administrators but are inert; revocation does not affect their area-based access.
Assignments grant and revoke project access for administrators as they do for operators.
Assignments naming administrators are refused, so every persisted assignment is effective.
open_points.default_guess: Treat administrator assignments as permitted but inert because M07 states that behavior most specifically.

witness.initial: An active administrator covers project P through the single administrative-area policy and has no assignment for P.
events: An administrator creates a StaffProjectAssignment from that administrator account to active project P.
The assigned administrator requests a read of P.
outcomes: Under M07, both assignment operations are inert and the administrator still reads P through administrative-area scope.
If State 0's grant/assignment invariants apply to every StaffProjectAssignment, the active assignment supplies access and its revocation blocks the next request.
witness.observer: The administrator making the project read and the administrator managing assignments.

open_points.subject: Initial ServicePrincipal status
open_points.text: M13 defines `status: PrincipalStatus (active | disabled)` and says “the only modification is the status change `active ↔ disabled`,” but does not state which status `create_service_principal` assigns.
open_points.question: Is a newly created ServicePrincipal initially active or disabled?
options: Created active and immediately able to authenticate after a credential is issued.
Created disabled and must be enabled before any credential can authenticate.
The administrator selects the initial status during creation.
open_points.default_guess: Create it active, matching the usual entry point implied by the lifecycle and the separate disable action.

witness.initial: An administrator is authorized to manage service principals for active project P.
events: The administrator grants it P and issues a credential.
The producer authenticates with that credential and imports a snapshot for P without any intervening status-change action.
outcomes: If creation enters `active`, the import can pass principal-status checking.
If creation enters `disabled`, the import is rejected until an administrator explicitly enables the principal.
witness.observer: The producer receiving the import result and the administrator provisioning the integration.

open_points.subject: Global producer authorization
open_points.text: State 0 says, “a global producer exists only through an explicitly granted capability,” and its common rule requires project access through a grant/assignment. M13 instead says, “With `all_projects` the scope mode alone admits an import for any project the Registry reports active; no grant is consulted and no further capability is needed.”
open_points.question: Does `scope_mode = all_projects` itself authorize every active project, or must a global producer also hold a separate explicitly granted global capability or project-access grant?
options: `all_projects` is the explicit global grant; the static import capability plus that scope mode is sufficient.
A separate global capability must be granted in addition to `all_projects`.
Even an `all_projects` principal must have a ProducerProjectGrant for each project.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the administrator-selected and audited `all_projects` scope mode as the explicit global grant, because M13 states that no further capability or grant is consulted.

witness.initial: Active Registry project P exists. An active ServicePrincipal has `scope_mode = all_projects`, a valid credential, the static snapshot-import capability, and no ProducerProjectGrant for P.
events: The producer submits a valid snapshot publication for P.
outcomes: Under M13, authorization succeeds because Registry reports P active and `all_projects` is sufficient.
Under State 0's literal global-capability and grant/assignment requirements, authorization fails because no separate global capability or project grant exists.
witness.observer: The producer receiving the import result and the administrator who configured its scope.

open_points.subject: Creation of imported plans and unmatched PortalSections versus pre-activation reallocation
open_points.text: The section says, “Activation of an imported version creates plans” and unmatched source sections create new `PortalSection` records, but also says allocations to absent previous sections “must be explicitly re-allocated by an operator before that version can be activated: activation is refused while any is unresolved.”
open_points.question: Which product action creates the candidate version’s SectionPlans and unmatched PortalSections early enough for operators to target them during the required pre-activation reallocation, and do those records survive a refused activation?
options: Candidate-version creation, not activation, creates all plans and unmatched PortalSections; activation only links, validates and changes status.
A first refused activation creates and retains the plans and PortalSections so reallocation can follow.

Activation creates them only in its successful transaction; unresolved allocations must instead be moved to already-existing sections or `other_expenses`, so unmatched new sections cannot receive allocations before activation.
open_points.default_guess: Create the imported plans and unmatched PortalSections when the imported candidate BudgetVersion is created, then make activation only validate resolution and switch status.

witness.initial: Project P has an active manual version with old section O, and expense E is allocated to O. An accepted snapshot candidate contains only unmatched source section N.
events: A staff member attempts to prepare the imported version for activation.
The staff member must explicitly reallocate E before activation.
The staff member tries to target N.
outcomes: If candidate creation already minted N and its plan, the staff member can reallocate E to N and then activate the version.

If activation alone mints N but refuses while E remains allocated to O, N does not yet exist as a target; the required reallocation cannot be completed unless a failed activation persists model records or E is diverted elsewhere.
witness.observer: The staff member preparing the budget transition and clients who later see E under N or under a different target.
